home.tagline: Every block can hold a world.
home.intro: A Fabric mod for Minecraft 26.3. Ten worlds, each sealed inside a single block and nested in the one before it. Every world has its own rule, its own creatures, its own station, and a boss guarding the core that opens the next.
home.facts: Minecraft 26.3 on Fabric, version 0.4.3. Solo and multiplayer.
home.dollsTitle: A set of eleven nesting dolls, just opened: the Surface, then worlds 1 to 10, from the largest to the smallest
home.dollsCaption: The Surface, then the ten worlds it holds. Pick a doll to open its world.
home.loopP: One loop, ten times over. Each pass asks you to unlearn the last world.

loop.p: Follow the Scroll's sketch to the Guardian's Sanctuary and beat the Block Guardian. It drops its core, the Matrix Workbench and your first World Soil.
At the Matrix Workbench: the last boss's core plus resources from its world. The World 1 Seed asks for the Guardian Core, 16 iron ingots and 16 oak logs.
Till World Soil with a hoe and plant the Seed, with water within four blocks. What you feed it decides whether its world hatches calm or wild.
The Seed hatches into a World Block. Use it and you shrink inside, onto a Threshold that brings you back out.
Toxin, heat, wind, noise, gravity, pressure: each world changes how you play. Its station turns local resources into the gear that answers the rule.

loop.h: Beat the boss, take its core
loop.p: Every attack is announced, then leaves an opening. Read the pattern, punish the opening, take the core.

The core opens the way into the next world, and every world has its own rite: an Ember Heart near lava, a key in an iron door, a rod in a storm, a lantern in the dark. Ten times, until the last block opens onto something much larger.

home.worldsP: Learning, then mastery, then expertise. World 10 tests everything at once.
home.sysP: Death teaches. It does not erase hours of progress.

systems.p: A nested doll you wear. When you die, a layer breaks instead and you get back up. It gains layers after Worlds 1, 5 and 8.
Every item holds a soul. At the Soul Altar, purify it for karma or devour it for power. Karma moves prices, quests and the ending.
Every weapon, tool and armour piece is born with one of six classes. Raise it to level 5 with souls, or gamble on a Chance Doll.
Up to eight players share a group, its worlds and its defeated bosses. Bosses grow tougher with every player who joins the fight.
Each class has three branches of four talents at the Class Table, bought with souls and Shell Shards and opened as your group goes deeper.
After an ending, race each world's trial or the Gauntlet of the eleven bosses for the server's board. In the worlds, invasions, surges of the rule and travelling merchants come and go.

verbs.p: Plant the first Seed, then perform each world's own rite: fire, a key, a storm, darkness, mirrors, the deep. The block that appears holds a world.
Toxic air, rising heat, total darkness, upside-down gravity: each world bends one rule.
Fifty creatures with their own attacks, and a boss that guards the core of the next world.
Each world has its station, its armour and its tools, the ones you need for the world below.

faq.a: Read the Artisan's Scroll you spawn with, then find the Guardian's Sanctuary on the Surface and wake the Block Guardian.

Smoke puffs mean the rite is still waiting: stand close and it tells you what it lacks. The World 1 Seed wants tilled World Soil 0 and water; each other object's description says where it goes and what it waits for.

faq.q: I died inside a world. Are my things gone?
faq.a: No. A death chest keeps them where you fell, and a Soul Cradle placed beforehand lets you wake up inside the world.
Yes, with the mod on the server and on every client. Up to eight players share a group, its worlds and its bosses.

faq.q: Does it work on Lunar Client?
faq.a: Through Lunar Client's Fabric profile for 26.3, with Fabric API and GeckoLib.

faq.q: Does it work with Sodium, Iris and minimaps?
faq.a: Yes. It was checked with Sodium, Iris, Xaero's Minimap and World Map, JourneyMap, VoxelMap and Traveler's Backpack. Xaero's cave view and radar switch off in the Lightless Deep, where they would show what the dark hides.

The Matriochka Pack, a Modrinth .mrpack with the mod, its libraries, Just Enough Items and client performance mods, in a normal and a hard version. It is attached to every GitHub release, with the optional Matriochka HD resource pack.
English, French, Spanish, German and Brazilian Portuguese: names, interface, quests, the Scroll, the fifty Journal pages, endings and subtitles.

faq.q: Can I fight a boss again?
faq.a: Yes. Its altar wakes it again, and it drops its core, soil and souls again.

bosses.lead: Eleven fights, each built the same way: an announcement you can read, a fast and dangerous attack, then an opening. Hit a boss during its opening and it takes 1.5 times the damage; outside of it, only three quarters. Every attack has its own animation: the boss shows the blow coming during the warning, strikes, then stays open and spent for exactly as long as the opening lasts. Each fight opens on a short cinematic: letterbox bars, the camera turning to the boss, its title card.

systems.lead: What keeps you alive, what you trade for power, how your gear grows, and what waits after the story. Everything here works the same in solo and on a server.
systems.desc: Doll of Life, death and respawn, souls and karma, gear classes and talents, new gear and station automation, groups, quests, trials, world events and comfort options in Matriochka.

lifeDoll.p: You carry a doll made of layers. It gets its first layer when the Spore Queen falls, a second after the Light Eater and a third after the Master of Seasons. Every boss you beat restores one layer, and the Soul Altar rebuilds one for 50 souls and 4 rare resources of the world you are in.

death: If your Doll of Life has a layer left, it breaks and you get back up on the spot. A doll can save you at most once a minute.
Otherwise you die, and a death chest keeps your inventory where you fell. It never despawns; inside a boss arena it waits at the entrance.
If you placed a charged Soul Cradle in that world, you wake up next to it.
If not, you are sent back outside, to your usual spawn point.

features.p: A small painted cradle that lets you respawn inside a world. It holds 3 charges; feed it one resource from that world and 5 souls to add another. One active cradle per player and per world.
Pulls you back to the World Block. You can also simply walk back onto the Threshold where you arrived.

Break a World Block and everyone inside is pushed out safely. The block becomes a Cracked Doll tied to that exact world: set it down again and the world comes back with its bases and chests, unstable for 20 minutes. It is also how you move a world.

systems.soulsLead: Every item carries a soul whose weight depends on its rarity. Put it on the Soul Altar and choose, for good: purify it to free the soul and gain karma, or devour it to absorb the soul and lose karma. Either way you keep the souls, which pay for class upgrades, talents, cradle charges and doll layers. Structure chests also keep Soul Shards (5 souls) and Soul Vessels (20), about 10 souls a chest.
systems.karmaNote: Karma runs from −100 to +100. An item gives one point of karma per 10 souls, and less each time you repeat the same offering. Quests with a choice move it by 5 or 10.

karma.p: The peoples welcome you. Mutual-help quests open up and the brighter world variants answer you.
Prices are 10% lower. People trust you.
Neither saint nor devourer. Every choice still counts.
Prices are 10% higher, but the first black market opens to you.
Some villages turn hostile. Pact quests and forbidden loot await.

systems.karmaEnd: At ±100, karma also tilts the variants of the worlds you open, and it decides between two of the three endings: seal the creature away, or absorb its power.
systems.classesLead: Every weapon, tool and armour piece gets a random class when it is crafted. The Class Table raises its level with souls and Shell Shards; your progression caps how far you can go.
systems.upNote: Level 1 to 5 costs 400 souls and 6 Shell Shards per piece (1, 1, 2, 2). Every boss leaves 3 Shell Shards to each player who fought it: enough to bring its world's weapon to the cap.

chance.p: Rerolls an item into a different class it can hold, and keeps its level. The first reroll costs 20 souls, and the price doubles each time on the same item: 20, 40, 80, 160.

systems.talentsLead: The Class Table also holds a cabinet of talent trees: three branches of four talents for each of the six classes, 72 in all. A branch is learnt in order; the first two talents cost souls, the last two souls and Shell Shards, and each tier opens as your group beats deeper bosses. A class's talents act while you wear or hold its gear (any tool counts for the Prospector).

systems.gearLead: 7 weapons and tools that behave like the world they come from, each crafted at its world's station and drawn by hand. They are born with a class like any other gear.

gear.p: Its arrows burst into a cloud of toxic spores where they strike. World 1.
Sets foes ablaze; every third blow bursts into a ring of flame. Swinging it warms you in the Veins. World 2.
Long reach. Every lash drags the foe toward you and slows it. World 3.
Use it to throw: lightning falls where it strikes, then it flies back to your hand. World 4.
Blocks like a shield. Each blocked blow flares: the attacker is blinded, thrown back and marked. World 5.
Use it to throw: it drags what it hits back to you, farther under water. Its line brings it home. World 7.
Mines a column of three. Use it on the ground: a tremor that staggers the creatures around you. World 9.

auto: Every station with recipes works with hoppers. It keeps one recipe: the last one crafted there by hand, or the one picked with the small gilded funnel that shows on a recipe under the cursor.
Ingredients go in from the top and the sides, each into its own slots; anything else is refused. The result comes out from below, and a comparator reads how full the station is.

Each station keeps its condition: heat for the Ash Foundry, a charge for the Lightning Forge (lightning, or Storm Essence in its fuel slot), darkness, deep water, dawn and dusk. The Spore Vat waits for a ripe brew, and the Jailer's Table makes one batch per lock pattern entered.
The Soul Altar and the Class Table stay manual. Breaking a station drops its buffer.

autoShot.caption: The stations' lit faces glow in the dark

shake.p: From outside, a player of the owning group can sneak and use the World Block with empty hands to help those inside: creatures stunned and thrown off their feet for 3 seconds, a boss staggered and open. Strike it with the Doll Mallet instead and the world quakes, loose blocks falling over their heads. One shake per world every 30 seconds.

systems.nestingLead: The name is the rule: something can always hold something else. These systems unlock as the story goes on.

nest.b: Three sizes: a chest holds the smaller ones and sorts items into them
A defeated mob releases a smaller one
A pocket base for your group, that grows after Worlds 5, 7 and 9
Lacquer Layers laid on armour: when the outer one breaks, the next takes over
Nested in order, the ten open World 0, the smallest doll

gates: Enchanting, anvils and the Nether open after World 2.
Diamonds come back in World 5: four Diamond Fragments make one at the Dark Altar. Until then villagers keep their diamond trades aside.
Elytra stay grounded in Worlds 4, 6 and 9 until World 8 is done.
systems.groupsLead: A player alone is a group of one. Worlds, progression and permissions belong to the group: up to eight players by default. Each group gets its own 3,000 by 3,000 block parcel in every world, walled off from the others, and a World Block can only be used by its group.

systems.serverNote: The mod runs on the server and on every client. All rules, damage and rewards are decided by the server; nothing needs an online account or service.
systems.journalLead: The Artisan's Scroll arrives on your first login and turns into the Journal when the Guardian falls. Its tabs track your objective, quests, karma and worlds. There are 70 optional quests (4 on the Surface, 6 per world and 6 on the paths of karma) and 100 achievements, 10 per world, two of them hidden. Fifty Journal pages, read in the Pages tab, and ten hidden dolls are scattered through the worlds; nest the dolls in order and something smaller opens. After the last boss, your karma chooses your ending, and a New Cycle starts the worlds over, stronger.

firstSteps.p: Until you enter World 1, a small lacquered card under the HUD plaque shows the next of ten steps, from reading the Scroll to planting the first Seed, with its item, a short hint and a compass needle toward the nearest Guardian's Sanctuary. Each step is detected from what you really do, and the Guide button on the Scroll or the Journal hides it.

systems.titlesNote: Titles are worn from the Trials book, quest titles included.
systems.trialsLead: Once you have seen an ending, the Trials open: a rush per world (two waves of its creatures, the second led by its elites, then its boss) and the Gauntlet of the eleven bosses, fought against the clock on a lacquered stage inside the Refuge doll, painted for each world. Open them from the Journal's Objective page, a Trial Altar or /matriochka trials start. Falling carries you out instead of killing you.

trialFacts.d: health and damage, ×1.2 / ×1.15 in the Gauntlet; always mutated, no introduction, no story reward
its Trophy Doll and a title

systems.board: A clock on the HUD runs green while you are under par. Best times are kept per player and per group, and the server keeps a board of the ten best groups for every trial, in the Trials book and with /matriochka trials top.
systems.eventsLead: While you are in a world, now and then something happens around you. A boss bar follows each event. Never in peaceful; operators can start one with /matriochka event.

events.p: 3 waves of the world's creatures, more for every player nearby; the last is led by a glowing warlord. A reward chest waits at the end.
The world's rule grows twice as strong for 2 minutes, with its own effect and particles. Ride it out for 15 souls.
A wanderer of the world's people sets up for a while, with special trades: its world's new gear, Shell Shards, rare pieces.

surges.p: The jungle exhales: toxin rises twice as fast and spore clouds drift by.

surges.name: Magma Surge
surges.p: The veins boil: heat rises twice as fast and the ground spits flame.

surges.name: Crushing Current

surges.name: Season Rush

surges.name: Unravelling
surges.p: The Workshop's seams give way: every zone's rule bites twice as hard.

systems.comfortLead: Opened from the Journal's Comfort button (or from Mod Menu), saved per player in config/matriochka-client.json.
comfort: Soft effects: no Nausea or Darkness, a gentle tint instead; the server skips those effects for you

A title card the first time you enter each world, with its rule medallion and a line about its law.
Phase breaks freeze the frame with a flash and the shell's number; heavy blows and moving ground shake the camera.
Adaptive music: a danger theme while creatures hunt you, boss themes, a heartbeat at low health or breath, and stings for a structure, a Journal page or a quest. Themes fade into one another.
systems.atmos: Every world has its own light, fog and particles: spore haze, falling embers, cold dust, a storm sky, near-black fog where a lantern reads across a cavern, an inverted pastel sky, deep blue water, light tinted by the season, rust haze, warm workshop light, and World 0's red lacquer dusk. Items, blocks and stations are hand-painted in the vanilla style, and their lit faces glow in the dark. Matriochka HD, an optional 32 x 32 resource pack, is attached to every release; Iris shader packs work through vanilla light.

steps: Follow your Scroll's sketch to the Guardian's Sanctuary on the Surface.
Use the sanctuary altar: the Block Guardian rises. No offering needed.
Sneak while using the altar to fight it again.

bosses.name: Block Guardian
cooldown: Signature attack at most every 20 seconds, 1 second sooner per phase.
Medium attack at most every 8 seconds, light attack every 4 seconds when you are close; both come a little sooner each phase.
Each phase makes it 10% faster.
bosses.souls: 100 souls for every player within 64 blocks
unlocks: Its core opens the way into World 1.
Your Scroll becomes the Artisan's Journal.
Your Doll of Life gets one layer back.
special: At half health it rebuilds itself from the arena and heals 10% of its health.
bosses.story: The Guardian falls. Its core, the Matrix Workbench plans and the first World Soil are yours. Your Scroll becomes the Journal.

quests.name: The First Guardian
